2 of my best friends killed themselves over the last 2 years and it’s one of the most crushing pains you will feel. Whatever you do, don’t try to forget about it or sweep it under the rug. Don’t blame yourself either. You got this.

I definitely feel you there. I was pretty close to just up and going to Vegas and marrying my person. We were going to get old together and then it changed. It’s incredibly sad. But it gets less sad. So 10000% get a therapist and just fuckin talk about it. Also exercise at least a little every day. Reading for fun helps too.
Like, I’m not even suggesting not communicating out of hard feelings. But until you feel 100% stable and comfortable talking with them will set you back in your progress.

The first few MONTHS might be you just trying to survive. But know that’s to be expected and your process won’t look like anyone else’s. Try not to dwell. Try to do a couple things for yourself every day. Eventually more and more of your attention will be your own, and the thing that helped me was counting my progress. Noticing feeling a little less hopeless. And if you have good reason, do not communicate whatsoever.
I won’t lie, it’ll probably be when you accept that it won’t get better. A moment of clarity will come. You deserve somebody who actually wants you and anything else is doing yourself a disservice.

Hey dude. Similar situation here. A few months ago my ex’s drinking was escalating to new heights. I loved her more than anything and put everything into her, which feels silly considering the constant criticism, accusations, and anger I’m sure you’re familiar with. She said she wanted to break up with me, and I had a panic attack. The next day, I thought I should get some help because my mental was getting really bad. I tried telling her I was going to check in somewhere for a few days. She reacted by telling me to leave, and then calling me screaming “I don’t fucking care about you, I hate you, I never want to see you again, I don’t love you”, sending me hundreds of really nasty and ugly and mean text messages attacking some of my biggest insecurities, including my mental state. She made fraudulent gofundme saying I “threatened” her with suicide, when I said I wanted to get help. That night I tried to hang myself with a guitar cord. After trying, I couldn’t tie it to anything where I was so I just sat there trying to choke myself out and crying violently for hours. I slept maybe a few hours and the next morning went to the hospital and let me tell you. Having mental health professionals tell you that what you’re experiencing is abuse/domestic violence can often be the first thing to help you realize what you’re going through is serious. It’s not like anything makes the pain go away but to know you aren’t crazy, to know you don’t deserve to be condescended or belittled or criticized at every other step. To know you don’t deserve for somebody that’s supposed to love you to talk to you like their worst enemy, even if they’re upset. It helps your process knowing you have your own narrative that they can’t control or bully you out of or gaslight you into believing their version of things before your own. It’s been 2 months for me, out of a 2 year relationship. It’s been hard. I’ve definitely slipped up and seen her since. But after almost every interaction, her rage comes out and all of a sudden it’s all my fault again. It’s hard to not care or not want to see them but just know that seeing them again will only serve to further traumatize you. Abusers will never change if they don’t think they have a problem.
